newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Heavy volumes propelled South African shares to a stronger close on Friday after a cagey start on Wall Street's overnight fall.
"Volumes were exceptionally exciting. About 928 million rands worth of shares went through," one trader said.

Dealers said market sentiment was overwhelmingly positive and much hunger was seen for heavyweight stocks, especially Richemont which saw 72 million rands worth of shares change hands. The share finished 250 cents up at 63.25 rand.
"Demand for heavyweights pushed industrials up. Richemont saw a great deal of interest," one dealer said.
Institutional buyers staged a return to the market after sitting on the sidelines for much of the week due to Wall Street's volatility.
A strong local bond market offered support to the equity market from the start but investors only began moving into equities around noon, dealers said.
Some futures arbitrage was seen, trying to close the widening gap between futures and there underlying stocks.
But traders said this futures activity was not as great as had been expected.
"There was very little basket-trading from the futures side," one dealer said.
A firm market was seen next week but all eyes remained on the Dow with players not yet convinced its downside had been beaten and its volatility eroding too much reliance on it to point the way.
"This trend could continue, but it all depends on Wall Street and I'm loathe to say we've completely discounted the Dow's correction. The downside on the Dow is not yet over," a dealer said.

Local economic indicators next week -- March CPI on Wednesday, March trade on Wednesday, March M3 money supply and private credit growth on Thursday -- were seen offering a slightly positive bias. Money supply would be watched most closely, dealers said.
Gold shares dipped to the close after trading slightly weaker on the day with the bullion price above $342 capping losses there.
Industrial shares added 77.6 points to 8,316.3 points, all-shares were up 46.2 points at 7,022.2 and golds were off 3.1 points to 1,247.3 points.

Malbak finished 120 cents higher at 23 rand following an announcment late Thursday that its major shareholder Sankorp had struck a tender offer deal on the shares to be involved in the unbundling of its listed firms.

The deal has been struck to give shareholders who do not want to keep the shares they receive in the unbundling the choice of selling them to the Public Investment Commissioners instead of into the market.
Carrig was up eight cents at 54 cents after its said that negotiations which could have an effect on the price of its shares were continuing.
Dries remained beleaguered by its dismal first quarter gold results and was down 180 cents to 39 rand.
Steers was up 10 cents to 230 cents after it said it planned to buy the businesses of Speciality Franchising Trust for a maximum consideration of 25 million rand.
Fresh market talk that Anglo American Corp of South Africa could sell their First National Bank stake thrust the bank's share upward in active trade, dealers said.

FNB shares jumped to a day's high of 31 rand before retreating slightly to 30.75 rand by 1518 GMT from a previous close of 29.75 rand -- 100 cents or 3.36 percent higher -- in a traded volume of 672,100 shares.

Shares in Randgold's Durban Roodepoort Deep Ltd, Buffelsfontein Gold Mines Ltd and Blyvooruitzicht Gold Mining Co Ltd rose on an announcement that the mines were considering proposals which analysts said could include plans to merge.
Near-dated stock futures also enjoyed good demand and held firmer levels, buoyed by the local bond marekt as well.
Gold contracts hardly budged all day, hampered by a dull bullion price.
The June industrial contract was last at 8,170/77 from 8,071 settlement, the all-share was at 6,511/18 from 6,478 and the gold contract was at 875/90 from 880.
-- Melanie Cheary, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
